source: CAMIL GE-V-04 · Page 08 · Health and Colors (health half)
notes: Page 08 carries two unrelated topics; health and colours are separate areas.
The page's six example sentences ('Doctor, I need to book an appointment') are excluded.
Four words dropped as harmful in current English: 'cripple' is a slur, 'handicapped' is
dated and avoided in favour of 'disabled', 'maimed' describes an injury rather than a
person, and 'hunchback' is a caricature. A learner who repeats them in an English-speaking
workplace damages their own standing, which is the opposite of what this course is for.
They are NOT taught as a unit. Every exercise type here makes the learner produce the
word — fill-in-the-blank hands them the sentence and waits for it, dictation has them
them as words to recognise and never use, which is prose and can carry the judgement
Two more dropped on other grounds: 'hunch' glossed as joroba, when the page's own example
sentence uses the common sense (presentimiento) — the same trap as 'sleep'/lagaña on page
07; and 'ailment', formal and the fourth word on the page meaning enfermedad.
'mute', 'cross-eyed' and 'one-eyed' are kept: dated rather than offensive.
sick/ill (enfermo, US against British) and ache/pain (dolor) are collision pairs and stay
VERY_EASY: an A1/A2 course, still its early pages.

The warning is appended to the paragraph by the seeder, not written by the model. Asked for it in the topic, the model dropped it silently: the A1 brief caps the paragraph at 60-90 words and spends them on the unit's own words.

area.name: Health and Illness
area.description: Hablar de cómo te sientes: estar sano o enfermo, los dolores y los síntomas, y qué encuentras en un hospital.

units.name: Health and illness
units.topic: Being well and being unwell. 'sick' and 'ill' both translate as enfermo — one is American, one British — and 'sickness', 'illness' and 'disease' are all enfermedad with real differences: a disease is a named medical condition, an illness is the state of being unwell, sickness leans towards nausea. The unit should make those differences clear

units.name: Aches and pains
units.topic: Saying where it hurts. 'ache' and 'pain' are both dolor and the unit should distinguish them: an ache is dull and lasting, a pain is sharper. The compound aches name the body part that hurts

units.name: Symptoms and remedies
units.topic: What you tell a doctor you are feeling, and the first thing you reach for

units.name: Sight, hearing and mobility
units.topic: The respectful, current English for disability: the words for not seeing, not hearing, not speaking and not being able to move, and the correct general word.

paragraphNote.en: You will sometimes hear the words "cripple", "handicapped" and "maimed". These words hurt people. Do not use them. Say "disabled".
paragraphNote.es: A veces vas a escuchar las palabras «cripple», «handicapped» y «maimed». Estas palabras ofenden. No las uses. Di «disabled».
